gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-mono: Stretched, spacious, and bold as a marker line. Noto Sans Mono follows with generously spaced letters and tall lowercase that make long paragraphs look sturdy against Warnes.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro packs dense, tall-bodied words with big entrances into each letter. Over a long page, Noto Sans Mro keeps that tight vertical rhythm going, while Warnes above looks drawn with one nib.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-multani: Noto Sans Multani reads lofty and light, its e leaving a wide gap at the terminal. And Warnes, with round letters that don't tilt, sits above it like a bold, stretched sign over a quiet shelf.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Heavy ink, wide stance, loud on purpose. Make Warnes small and its outline-like strokes lose their swagger, while Noto Sans Myanmar, with its thick band of text and broad-mouthed c, would feel ponderous if set large.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Warnes draws every stroke as stout as a pipe cleaner, stretched wide with tapering ends. And Noto Sans Nabataean, whose lowercase nearly reaches cap height, can stay modest in size without losing presence.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Warnes is stretched and swaggering, with no swelling where its curves meet the stems. Noto Sans Nag Mundari matches it with big, half-unwrapped c and s shapes.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Warnes makes its r, n and m with arches that match their stems, all stretched wide and bold. Noto Sans Nandinagari stays friendly, with short ascenders.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-newa: Warnes has no thick-thin modulation at all, just bold ink strokes tapering out before they touch. And Noto Sans Newa, with its open-mouthed e and tall bowls, would carry a long passage with an easy, upright flow.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Towering lowercase, with terminals held far off the stroke body. Noto Sans Nushu can stay quite small before it loses presence, and Warnes above it is hollow glass-tube lettering.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham has wide-gapped e shapes and tall bodies. Down a long passage, those tall lowercase forms look bold, while Warnes keeps crossbars as thick as its stems.
